items.headline: Romania Farmers’ Protest Turns Violent Amid Provocation Claims
items.summary: A farmers’ protest in the Romanian capital erupted in violence on Tuesday when demonstrators spurred on by alleged agitators clashed with riot police, in the worst civil unrest the country has seen in years.
items.author: Andra Timu and Irina Vilcu

items.headline: Reform Considers European Court in Fight to Keep Record Gift
items.summary: Reform UK is considering a legal challenge under the European Convention on Human Rights if the Labour government’s bid to retroactively cap overseas political donations is successful.
items.author: Lucy White

items.headline: Brazil Top Court Judges Battle Over Probe Into Powerful Justice
items.summary: Members of Brazil’s Supreme Court battled over whether to open an unprecedented investigation into one of their fellow justices Tuesday, accusing each other of political bias and spreading falsehoods in a fiery public hearing.
items.author: Daniel Carvalho, Martha Beck and Beatriz Reis

items.headline: Merz Calls for Trade Tools to Fight ‘Unfair’ China Competition
items.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz said that Germany will support tough new measures against China’s “unfair” trade practices at a meeting of European Union leaders next month.
items.author: Arne Delfs

items.headline: Bessent to Meet Chinese Counterpart Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he will meet this weekend with his Chinese counterpart, He Lifeng, ahead of a summit between President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping later this month.
items.author: Yash Roy

items.headline: Canada's Carney Expands Tax Breaks for Most New Capital Investing
items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says the government is expanding the scope of a major investment tax write-off to include oil and gas pipelines, mining property, and more. He made the announcement at an investment summit in Toronto. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Bessent Hearing Repeatedly Interrupted by Protesters
items.summary: Protesters repeatedly stood up and interrupted US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's testimony on Capitol Hill Tuesday. He is testifying about the state of the international financial system before the House Financial Services Committee. Police stepped in and took the protesters out of the room without incident. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Bessent Says He’ll Meet With China's He Lifeng This Weekend
items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the UAE has made forward-leaning moves against Iran-linked finance, including cutting off financial transactions and trade with Iran. He speaks during testimony before the House Financial Services Committee. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Fed Has to Put Up or Shut Up, Says DoubleLine's Sherman
items.summary: DoubleLine Capital Deputy Chief Investment Officer Jeffrey Sherman says it's time for the Federal Reserve to "put up or shut up." With bond yields trading above 5%, he says "the best thing to do is bring a hike." Sherman speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: UAE Working to Be Removed From Foreign Travel Warning Lists
items.summary: The United Arab Emirates is working with other countries on removal from their travel advisory lists just as hotel occupancies in Dubai rebound to their highest since the Iran war started.
items.author: Kateryna Kadabashy and Abeer Abu Omar

items.headline: Bessent Says He’s Supportive of $5,000 Checks for Americans
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he’s supportive of a plan floated by President Donald Trump to send $5,000 checks to American adults if Republicans retain their majorities in Congress, downplaying concerns about the potential cost.
items.author: Yash Roy

items.headline: MBS and Saudi Arabia Face Crisis With Key Oil Pipeline Shut for Weeks
items.summary: The US-Iran war has reached crisis point for Saudi Arabia and its de facto leader, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
items.author: Mirette Magdy, Fiona MacDonald, Veena Ali-Khan and Alex Wickham

items.headline: Trump's Intent on $5,000 Checks Is Very Real, Bessent Says
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the Treasury is looking at President Donald Trump's proposal to give each American adult $5,000 if Republicans keep control of Congress after the November elections. He says President Trump's intent is very real. Bessent testifies before the House Financial Services Committee. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Bessent Accuses Democrats of 'Poisoning' Consumer Data
items.summary: US Representative Jim Himes (D-CT) pushes back on optimistic claims about the economy, arguing that upbeat rhetoric amounts to political malpractice when consumer sentiment has fallen sharply. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: NYC Postpones Vote on Property-Tax Break for Hudson Yards Tower
items.summary: New York City put off voting on a $100 million property tax break for a new Hudson Yards skyscraper proposed by developer Tishman Speyer, in what would be the largest economic subsidy since Mayor Zohran Mamdani took office.
items.author: Martin Z. Braun

items.headline: Bessent Says US Used 'Nominal' Amount for Yen Intervention
items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the Treasury’s engagement with Japan over currency intervention was part of a constant dialogue and that Japan’s finance ministry is very transparent with the U.S. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Patel Declines to Rule Out FBI Agents at Polls on Election Day
items.summary: FBI Director Kash Patel declined to rule out sending agents to polling places on Election Day, telling senators he wasn’t certain the bureau is legally barred from doing so.
items.author: Myles Miller

items.headline: Merz Cancels UN Trip to Address CDU Party Rebellion in Berlin
items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz cancelled his trip to the United Nations General Assembly in New York next week, changing course as he works to contain an open rebellion of his own party in Berlin.
items.author: Arne Delfs

items.headline: War in Iran Has Cost US $38 Billion Over Five Months, CBO Says
items.summary: President Donald Trump’s decision to go to war against Iran has cost US taxpayers about $38 billion in direct costs during the first five months of fighting and will push inflation up about 0.5 percentage points by early next year, a new congressional study finds.
items.author: Gregory Korte and Erik Wasson

items.headline: Trump’s Kennedy Center Board Votes to Close Facility for Repairs
items.summary: The board of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts voted Tuesday to close the facility for repairs, according to people familiar with the decision.
items.author: Jeff Mason
